headline: Your mobile app, from the brief to the store
lede: I build software from Belém, in northern Brazil, and have done since 2020. You come with an app to build, a codebase somebody else wrote and nobody wants to open, or a library you would rather license than rebuild. From the first email to the handover, you deal with me.
chips: Apps published to Google Play and the Microsoft Store
Code, credentials and store accounts are yours at the end

offeringsNote: Three shapes of work: something built from a scope written down before it starts, a licence for something already published and maintained, and a second reading of something that already exists.

offerings.title: A mobile app, built and shipped
offerings.description: Your app from the brief to a listing live on the store. I have handled store submission inside companies since 2019.
bullets: Flutter and React Native, with native Kotlin and Swift where your app needs it
Publishing to Google Play and the App Store, including answering the review team when they reject a build
Firebase, CI/CD pipelines and automated tests set up with the project
Native modules in Swift, Objective-C, Java and Kotlin, bridged into the React Native codebase you already have
offerings.linkLabel: Mobile development in Flutter and React Native

offerings.title: A licence for something already built
offerings.description: License a package or an app I already maintain, instead of paying to have it built again and then waiting for it.

offerings.title: A second pair of eyes on your codebase
offerings.description: Your app is failing store review, or the developer who built it left. I read the codebase and work with the team that keeps it running.

Architecture review of your React Native or Flutter codebase, with the findings written down
Release engineering: pipelines, feature flags and staged rollouts
One to one mentoring for the engineers who will own the code after I leave

audienceTitle: Who this works for, and who it does not
audienceNote: Three cases that work well, and three I turn down. Better you know now than after signing.

audience.title: A project with a closed scope
audience.detail: You know roughly what the app has to do, and you want a price, a deadline and a list of exclusions in writing before anything starts.

audience.title: A codebase somebody else wrote
audience.detail: Your app is failing store review, or the developer who built it is gone and nobody left on the team has opened the project. I read it and tell you what I find.

audience.title: A licence and support for something already published
audience.detail: You need a library or an app that already exists and is already maintained, and you would rather license it than pay to have it built a second time.

audience.title: Not this: a developer allocated to your squad
audience.detail: I do not sell headcount or full-time availability. I do the work, and the calendar is agreed project by project.

audience.title: Not this: hourly work with no scope
audience.detail: With no written scope and no definition of done, the conversation ends up being about the invoice. With one, you know the price before anything starts and I know when I am finished.

processNote: The same four steps on every contract.

process.title: Scope
process.detail: You describe the problem. I come back with what I understood, what I would build and what I would deliberately leave out. That first pass is free and binds you to nothing.

process.title: Written estimate
process.detail: Price, deadline and everything outside the scope, in writing. Nothing starts before you have that document.

process.title: Iterative delivery
process.detail: Builds you can install and open, on a fixed cadence. You see your app running long before it is finished.

process.title: Handover
process.detail: Source code, credentials, store accounts and documentation are yours at the end. Support after that is a separate agreement you choose to sign.
